problems.problem: The painted wall shape is still not the bottle's own contour enlarged. Evidence: the charcoal form (approx x250-835, y320-920) is a squat jug/tag outline ~585px wide by ~600px tall (aspect ~0.97) while the real bottle is ~180px wide by ~650px tall (aspect ~0.28); its neck is a straight trapezoid and the body sides run straight with no cinched waist or base flare, so no viewer can read it as the same curve. The recognition event 'the contour answers its own name' therefore remains invisible. Root cause: background prompt described the contour in words but generation returned a generic wide vessel slab. Affected layer: scene. Repair: regenerate with a shape description that encodes the proportion (very tall narrow silhouette, width about one third of height, waisted midsection, flared foot) without naming the product.
problems.root_cause: generated wall graphic ignores the slender contour proportion and waist curve declared by the concept
problems.repair_strategy: regenerate background prompt specifying an extremely narrow tall flat painted contour with waist cinch and flared foot, proportion ~1:3.5 width:height

problems.problem: The declared counterpoint seam is broken: the painted shape's bottom edge stops at y~920, a pale wall band (~100px) remains between it and the wall-floor junction (~y1020), and the real bottle (base y1161) extends ~240px below the shape instead of visually filling its lower half. Evidence: visible light gap under the charcoal slab and bottle base standing on open floor well below the shape. The concept requires the silhouette to rise from the floor line so the standing cutout occupies its lower section. Root cause: shape placed and cropped mid-wall by the generator. Affected layer: scene. Repair: same regeneration, stating the painted contour meets the floor line and towers above the standing object's height.
problems.root_cause: painted contour does not reach the floor line, so object-to-silhouette alignment cannot register
problems.repair_strategy: include 'shape base coincides with the wall-floor junction line' in the regenerated prompt

problems.problem: The wall renders noticeably lighter and cooler (near-white, approx #DCDCDA in the upper field) than the declared matte mineral grey #C9C6C0, flattening the tonal plan: the charcoal shape and the dark ink now sit on an almost white field, losing the muted mineral mood of the concept and reducing the shape's matte paint presence. Evidence: side-by-side with the spec palette and the previous revision's grey; current wall reads white-grey with a faint cool cast. Root cause: 'pale ... no vignette' wording pushed value up during regeneration. Affected layer: scene. Repair: restate the exact mid-light mineral grey value and matte paint texture in the prompt while keeping even diffuse light.
problems.root_cause: regeneration over-lightened the wall value away from the palette grey
problems.repair_strategy: regenerate with explicit mid-light warm-grey mineral paint value, even diffuse frontal overhead light, no vignette

problems.problem: With the silhouette mis-proportioned and floating, the hero bottle (height ratio 0.4514, within the 0.35-0.74 policy) still reads as a small object in a large empty room: wide dead wall bands left (x0-250) and right (x835-1080) and a tall empty floor apron (y1161-1440) carry no compositional charge, unlike references 3-5 where the subject or its graphic field commands the frame. This is an artistic hierarchy concern, not a size-rule violation. Root cause: the missing alignment event leaves negative space unmotivated. Affected layer: composition. Repair: once the contour renders at correct proportion and floor contact, the paired shapes will activate the negative space; no product resize needed if the event lands.
problems.root_cause: visual event absent so declared negative space reads as emptiness
problems.repair_strategy: fix background contour first; reassess scale only if hierarchy remains thin
